parsed_output.analysis:
The model was checked against each numbered requirement in the specification.

Req 1: Human driving mode as simple state — satisfied (HumanDrivingMode is a plain state).
Req 2: Autonomous mode as sub-machine state — satisfied (AutonomousMode contains sub-states).
Req 3: "when power on, the system turn into human driving mode" — the model's initial transition [*] -> HumanDrivingMode has no guard/trigger at all, so "power on" is never explicitly modeled as the triggering event of the initial transition. This is a minor/moderate omission since the spec explicitly ties the initial transition to a "power on" event.
Req 4 (labeled "4" twice in spec, likely a typo duplicating numbering): "when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state" — modeled correctly as HumanDrivingMode -> AutonomousMode: front_distance > 10.
Req 4 (second bullet): "transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)" — this phrasing suggests the transition back to human driving mode should occur specifically when in the AutoFinal state (i.e., only from AutoFinalState), not from the general operational state. However the model has this transition defined from BOTH AutoOperationalState and AutoFinalState to HumanDrivingMode, which contradicts the "in (auto final)" qualifier that seems to restrict this transition to being valid only when the system is in the final substate.
Req 5: "when power off, it will transit to final state" — modeled as HumanDrivingMode -> [*] and AutonomousMode -> [*] with trigger "Power Off". This satisfies the requirement for both top-level states, which seems reasonable given the spec doesn't restrict which state must observe the power-off event.

Additional observations:
- The sub-state region has an internal AutoInitialState -> AutoOperationalState transition guarded by "Signal Transmission Succeeds", and AutoOperationalState -> AutoFinalState guarded by "Mission Completed" — these are not mentioned in the specification, so they are extraneous inventions not backed by the spec text. This might be seen as an unsupported elaboration beyond what's given.
- The naming "AutoInitialState", "AutoOperationalState", "AutoFinalState" with the qualifier "(auto final)" strongly suggests that only AutoFinalState should have the outgoing transition to HumanDrivingMode, meaning the AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode transition is likely an error introducing extra/inconsistent behavior not specified.
</analysis>
<issues>
<issue>
<where>Initial transition [*] -> HumanDrivingMode</where>
<issue>Missing "Power On" trigger on the initial transition</issue>
<reason>The spec states "when power on, the system turn into human driving mode", explicitly tying the transition from the initial pseudostate to HumanDrivingMode to a power-on event. In the model, this transition has no label/trigger at all, so the power-on condition required by the specification is not represented.</reason>
</issue>
<issue>
<where>AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed</where>
<issue>Transition to Human Driving Mode is defined from AutoOperationalState in addition to AutoFinalState</issue>
<reason>The specification says the transition to human driving mode on "human steering cmd, brake pressed" should occur "in (auto final)", implying this transition is only valid while the autonomous sub-machine is in its final state (AutoFinalState). By also allowing this transition directly from AutoOperationalState, the model introduces behavior not specified and effectively bypasses the "auto final" condition stated in the spec.</reason>
</issue>
<issue>
<where>Sub-states of AutonomousMode: AutoInitialState -> AutoOperationalState ("Signal Transmission Succeeds") and AutoOperationalState -> AutoFinalState ("Mission Completed")</where>
<issue>Internal transitions and their trigger names are not present in or derivable from the specification</issue>
<reason>The specification only describes the overall automaton behavior (entering/exiting autonomous mode, human/steering/brake events, power on/off); it gives no detail about internal sub-state transitions, their names, or their triggering conditions ("Signal Transmission Succeeds", "Mission Completed"). These are unsupported additions beyond the stated requirements, representing a mismatch between the modeled level of detail and what the spec actually specifies.</reason>
</issue>
<issue>
<where>AutonomousMode -> [*]: Power Off</where>
<issue>Power-off transition to final state defined directly on the composite AutonomousMode state, duplicating/overlapping with HumanDrivingMode's Power Off transition</issue>
<reason>The specification states "when power off, it will transit to final state" without clarifying whether this applies independently in both modes or only from Human Driving Mode (implying the system must first return to human driving mode before powering off). Having two separate Power Off exits (one from AutonomousMode and one from HumanDrivingMode) is an interpretive choice not explicitly justified by the spec text, and may not match the intended single power-off pathway.</reason>
</issue>
</issues>
</NaiveReview>

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] -> HumanDrivingMode
HumanDrivingMode: Human Driving Mode
HumanDrivingMode -> AutonomousMode: front_distance > 10
AutonomousMode: Autonomous Mode
state AutonomousMode {
[*] -> AutoInitialState
AutoInitialState: Initial State
AutoInitialState -> AutoOperationalState: Signal Transmission Succeeds
AutoOperationalState: Operational State
AutoOperationalState -> AutoFinalState: Mission Completed
AutoFinalState: Final State
AutoOperationalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
AutoFinalState -> HumanDrivingMode: human steering cmd, brake pressed
}
HumanDrivingMode -> [*]: Power Off
AutonomousMode -> [*]: Power Off
@enduml
